9. Series of Functions & Fourier

When series of functions converge uniformly — plus Fourier series and the Gibbs phenomenon.

  • The Weierstrass M-Test — If a majorant MnM_nMn​ dominates every term at all xxx and ∑Mn\sum M_n∑Mn​ converges, the series converges uniformly — here ∣sin⁡(nx)n2∣≤1n2=:Mn\left|\frac{\sin(nx)}{n^2}\right| \le \frac{1}{n^2} =: M_n​n2sin(nx)​​≤n21​=:Mn​ and ∑Mn=π26\sum M_n = \frac{\pi^2}{6}∑Mn​=6π2​, so the partial-sum error band tightens across the whole xxx-interval at once.
  • Dini's Theorem — On a compact set, a monotone sequence of continuous functions converging pointwise converges uniformly — a finite subcover of the open sets EnE_nEn​ grabs them all at once. The twin tool of the M-test.
  • The Ringing That Never Dies — Layer sine waves onto a square wave. The ringing beside each jump never dies out, no matter how large NNN gets.
  • Riemann–Lebesgue Lemma — Fourier coefficients die out — ∫f(x)sin⁡(nx) dx→0\int f(x)\sin(nx)\,dx \to 0∫f(x)sin(nx)dx→0. Rapid oscillation averages away every bump of fff.
  • Fejér's Theorem — The Cesàro means σN\sigma_NσN​ of Fourier partial sums converge uniformly for continuous functions — because the Fejér kernel is an approximate identity. Overlay the ringing SNS_NSN​ with the smooth σN\sigma_NσN​.
  • Parseval's Identity — Energy is conserved — 1π∫−ππ∣f∣2=a022+∑(an2+bn2)\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |f|^2 = \frac{a_0^2}{2} + \sum (a_n^2 + b_n^2)π1​∫−ππ​∣f∣2=2a02​​+∑(an2​+bn2​). Watch the fraction of energy captured by the first NNN modes.
  • The Gibbs Phenomenon — Why the bump beside the jump never dies — rescaling by t=2Nxt = 2Nxt=2Nx collapses SNS_NSN​ onto (2/π)Si(t)(2/\pi)\mathrm{Si}(t)(2/π)Si(t), and the first peak tends to (2/π)Si(π)≈1.179(2/\pi)\mathrm{Si}(\pi) \approx 1.179(2/π)Si(π)≈1.179. The overshoot is about 8.95% of the jump.
